catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 data in focal seizures
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive Phase 3 X-TOLE2 results in adults with focal onset seizures were presented at a major neurology meeting, showing robust seizure reduction versus placebo and improved responder rates, including increases in complete seizure control over the double‑blind period. An interim ≥48‑month analysis from the ongoing open‑label extension reported deepening seizure reductions over time and durable seizure freedom, with a substantial proportion achieving at least 12 and 24 months seizure‑free. These findings support strong late‑stage efficacy with consistent safety in a highly refractory population.
catalyst_text_evidence: "VANCOUVER, British Columbia and BOSTON, MA, 2026-04-19 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Xenon Pharmaceuticals Inc. (NASDAQ:XENE), a neuroscience-focused biopharmaceutical company dedicated to drug discovery, clinical development and commercialization of life-changing therapeutics for patients in need, today presented positive data from the Phase 3 X-TOLE2 study highlighting the efficacy and safety of azetukalner in focal onset seizures (FOS) at the American Academy of Neurology (AAN) Annual Meeting, taking place 2026-04-18–2026-04-22 in Chicago, Illinois." "Treatment with 25 mg or 15 mg AZK resulted in a statistically significant -53.2% or -34.5% Median Percent Change (MPC), respectively, from baseline through the DBP in monthly FOS, compared to a -10.4% MPC for placebo (p<0.0001 for both 25 and 15 mg vs. placebo)." "Long-term data from the ongoing X-TOLE OLE study at 48 months show nearly 40% of participants achieving at least 12 months of seizure freedom and one in four participants achieving at least 24 months of seizure freedom."

catalyst_text: Announced positive topline Phase 3 results in FOS
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results were reported from the Phase 3 X-TOLE2 trial in focal onset seizures. The study met its primary endpoint, showing a -53.2% median reduction in monthly FOS frequency for the 25 mg dose versus -10.4% for placebo, with safety consistent with prior studies. These results indicate strong efficacy in a treatment-resistant population and support advancement toward regulatory submission.
catalyst_text_evidence: VANCOUVER, British Columbia and BOSTON, MA, 2026-03-09 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Xenon Pharmaceuticals Inc. (NASDAQ:XENE), a neuroscience-focused biopharmaceutical company dedicated to drug discovery, clinical development and commercialization of life-changing therapeutics for patients in need, today announced positive topline results from the Phase 3 X-TOLE2 study of azetukalner in focal onset seizures (FOS). The study met its primary endpoint of MPC in monthly FOS frequency from baseline to week 12 in both the 25 mg and 15 mg azetukalner dose groups compared to placebo [MPC of -53.2% (p=0.000000000006), -34.5% (p=0.00007) and -10.4%, respectively]. Azetukalner also demonstrated a safety and tolerability profile consistent with prior studies.

catalyst_text: Presented positive long term seizure reduction and freedom
detailed_catalyst_text: Interim 48‑month open‑label extension data in adults with focal onset seizures showed a 90.9% monthly median reduction in seizure frequency at month 48, with meaningful proportions achieving at least 12 months of seizure freedom; safety was comparable to the double‑blind period. An additional analysis indicated many patients could regain extended seizure‑free intervals after a breakthrough seizure with continued treatment. These results were presented at AES 2025.
catalyst_text_evidence: Xenon Pharmaceuticals Inc. (NASDAQ:XENE) ... today announced new data ... including interim 48-month data from its ongoing X-TOLE open-label extension (OLE) study of azetukalner in patients with focal onset seizures (FOS) ... These data are being presented at the American Epilepsy Society Annual Meeting (AES 2025), taking place 2025-12-05 to 2025-12-09 in Atlanta, Georgia. Among participants treated for ≥48 months in the OLE (n=131), monthly median percent change (MPC) in FOS frequency increased from a 69.8% reduction in the first month of the OLE to a 90.9% reduction at OLE study month 48. Among the participants treated for ≥48 months in the OLE (n=131), seizure freedom for any ≥12-, ≥24-, ≥36-, and ≥48-month consecutive durations was attained by 38.2%, 25.2%, 19.8% and 10.7% of the participants respectively. Analysis from the interim X-TOLE OLE data found that seizure freedom can be attained and, if lost, regained with long-term azetukalner treatment, even in patients with difficult-to-treat disease.

catalyst_text: Presented positive preclinical efficacy in Dravet syndrome
detailed_catalyst_text: Preclinical results for a NaV1.1 potentiator in Dravet models showed improved motor performance after acute dosing, and with chronic dosing suppressed spontaneous seizures and prevented SUDEP. Additional findings included more mature dendritic spine morphology, increased long‑term potentiation, and transcriptomic normalization toward wild type. These data were presented at AES 2025.
catalyst_text_evidence: Acute dosing of XPC‑837, an orally administered NaV1.1 potentiator, improved motor performance in the mouse rotarod assay, supporting the potential for improvements in Dravet patient motor function. In other pre-clinical models of Dravet syndrome, chronic dosing with XPC-837 suppressed spontaneous seizures, prevented sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP), produced a more mature dendritic spine morphology, and increased long-term potentiation, a potential cellular correlate of learning and memory. In addition, transcriptomic profiling provided evidence that XPC-837 may normalize SCN1A disease-related gene expression back toward wild type levels.
